recipe.name: Captcha Solver
test: env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME .venv/bin/python preflight.py && env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME .venv/bin/python -c "import ast,pathlib; [ast.parse(p.read_text()) for p in pathlib.Path('.').glob('*/*.py')]" && echo SYNTAX_OK

env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME .venv/bin/python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); import turnstile.solve, cloudflare.solve, awswaf.solve, botguard.solve, datadome.solve, perimeterx.solve, akamai.solve, recaptcha.solve, hcaptcha.solve; print('IMPORTS_OK')"
evidence: preflight.py asserts the browser build this solver resolves is present, executable and launchable, and honours CLOAKBROWSER_BINARY_PATH when set.
Syntax phase: all *.py under the solver packages must parse; a bad edit in a solver would otherwise only surface when that captcha type is requested.
Import phase: every browser solver module must import cleanly; this catches the concurrency refactor (solve_slot import) breaking a module.

No live /solve call in the recipe: solving needs network + a real captcha target, is slow and non-deterministic, and the service runs as a systemd unit. Live checks live in tools/bench_parallel.py and tools/smoke_all_types.py, run manually.
.venv is python 3.14 with --system-site-packages (needs the user-site cloakbrowser wrapper).
